Problem:
Entire requires per-repository setup (.entire/settings.json) to track agent sessions. Users managing multiple repos with Entire wanted a way to enable tracking globally across all their repos without configuring each one individually.
Solution:
Added a user-global settings tier in ~/.config/entire/settings.json that auto-enables Entire in any repository without repo-level setup. The feature includes:
Global config structure with enabled flag and two exclude lists:
exclude_paths: doublestar globs (with ~ expansion) to skip specific directories
exclude_origins: doublestar globs matching normalized host/owner/repo origins to exclude repos from specific sources
New gitremote.GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet() helper to look up all configured URLs for a remote, distinguishing between "not configured" and lookup errors — used to check whether a repo's origin matches an exclusion pattern.
Core predicate IsActiveForRepo() that hooks now use instead of IsSetUpAndEnabled(). It checks repo-level setup first (making explicit repo-level disable veto global mode), then falls back to global-mode activation if the repo has no setup.
Comprehensive exclusion matching with case-insensitive path folding on macOS/Windows (where filesystems are case-insensitive), and case-insensitive origin matching. Invalid exclude patterns are skipped so one bad entry doesn't break the list.
Fail-closed safety: all errors during global-mode checks (unreadable settings, missing worktree root, origin lookup failure) disable global mode to prevent silent misbehavior.
Hook entry points now consult the global tier at both gates (registry dispatch and git-command initialization), ensuring global repos get session logging and redaction like repo-level setups do.

All 13 findings on trail #1012 are resolved, so I re-reviewed the branch from scratch. First, verification that Monday's three fixes hold end-to-end through a real binary (not just unit tests) — probe repos + a temp `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, using `.entire/` creation as the activity signal:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `https://github.com/acme/widgets/` vs `exclude_origins: [github.com/acme/widgets]` | excluded ✓ |
| `git@github.com:acme/widgets.GIT` | excluded ✓ |
| `…/widgets.git/` vs `github.com/acme/*` | excluded ✓ |
| `exclude_origins: ["["]`, repo with **no** origin | fail-closed ✓ |
| `remote.origin.url=` (blank value) | fail-closed ✓ |
| unknown key in settings.json | fail-closed ✓ |
| no-origin repo, `github.com/**` | active (as documented) ✓ |
| `exclude_paths_exact` parent vs nested repo | parent inactive, nested active ✓ |

`mise run lint` clean; settings + gitremote suites and all six new gate tests pass.

Five new findings.

**1 — medium: global mode writes an *unignored* log into repos the user never set up; the next `git add -A` commits it.**
`initHookLogging` (`cmd/entire/cli/hooks_git_cmd.go:136`) now passes for global-tier repos and calls `logging.Init`, creating `.entire/logs/entire.log`. Nothing on the git-hook path calls `strategy.EnsureEntireGitignore` — that lives in `strategy.EnsureSetup`, reached only from the agent TurnStart handler (`lifecycle.go:604`) and `entire enable`. Under repo-level setup the ignore file always predates the first hook; under global mode a plain `git commit` in a repo where no agent turn has happened yet does not.

One new finding this pass, and it's the most serious so far — `01M0DX240HT6` (High), `strategy/common.go:110`.

**Global mode modifies tracked files in repos the user never set up.** `EnsureSetup` → `InstallGitHook` resolves its target via `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which honors `core.hooksPath`. When that points into the worktree — the widespread `.githooks` convention, or husky ≤ v8 where `.husky` is tracked — Entire renames the user's hooks to `*.pre-entire` and writes chaining wrappers over tracked paths. Verified with a tracked `.husky` + `core.hooksPath=.husky`: one agent TurnStart in a repo with no `.entire/` produced

```
 M .husky/commit-msg
 M .husky/pre-push
?? .husky/commit-msg.pre-entire  ?? .husky/pre-push.pre-entire
?? .husky/post-commit  ?? .husky/post-rewrite  ?? .husky/prepare-commit-msg
```

The "Backed up existing…" notices go to hook stderr, which nobody reads, and the next `git add -A` publishes those wrappers to a shared repo. Hook behavior is preserved (the wrappers chain to the backups), so this is about unsolicited changes to tracked files rather than breakage. With `core.hooksPath` unset it all lands in `.git/hooks` and is invisible to git — that's why this specific configuration is the sharp edge, and nothing in the codebase detects it (only the `ENOTDIR` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` check).

Two things I checked this pass that came back **clean**, so no findings:

- **Pre-push doesn't break pushes.** I expected global mode to risk aborting `git push` when a forge rejects `entire/checkpoints/v1`. It doesn't: `prePush` only returns errors for privacy-critical OPF failures (`hooks_git_cmd.go:334-350`), so a rejected checkpoint push leaves the user's push alone.

func TestZZRaceProbe(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)
	hooksDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "hooks")
	userHook := "#!/bin/sh\necho USER_HOOK_RAN\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(hooksDir, "commit-msg"), []byte(userHook), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Chdir(dir)

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			_, _ = InstallGitHook(t.Context(), true, false, false)
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()

	final, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(hooksDir, "commit-msg"))
	backup, berr := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(hooksDir, "commit-msg.pre-entire"))
	chained := strings.Contains(string(final), "commit-msg.pre-entire")
	backupIsUserHook := berr == nil && string(backup) == userHook
	backupIsEntireWrapper := berr == nil && strings.Contains(string(backup), "Entire CLI hooks")

	t.Logf("final-chains-to-backup=%v backup-is-user-hook=%v backup-is-entire-wrapper=%v", chained, backupIsUserHook, backupIsEntireWrapper)
	switch {
	case backupIsEntireWrapper:
		t.Errorf("LOST: user hook destroyed; backup holds Entire's own wrapper (recursive chain)")
	case backupIsUserHook && !chained:
		t.Errorf("ORPHANED: user hook preserved in backup but final hook does not chain to it — user hook never runs again")
	case !backupIsUserHook:
		t.Errorf("MISSING BACKUP: user hook not preserved (err=%v)", berr)
	}
}

The user's hook is gone from both files, and the installed hook now chains to a copy of itself, so every later `git commit` re-executes the same script until it hits a process or CPU limit.

Evidence: 5/12 runs with 8 concurrent in-process installs; 2/5 rounds with 8 parallel real `entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit` processes on this branch; 3/6 rounds against a binary built from split B's tip.

The failing test is written, RED, and lint-clean. The trail update didn't land, though — see the note at the end.

**`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks_concurrent_install_test.go`** (uncommitted, one new file, nothing else touched):

`TestInstallGitHook_ConcurrentInstallPreservesUserHook` seeds a user script for **every** `buildHookSpecs` entry (derived from the production helper, so it can't drift), runs 4 concurrent `InstallGitHook` calls per round across 120 rounds, and asserts per hook that (a) the backup still holds the user's script rather than an Entire wrapper, and (b) the installed hook chains to that backup — the two assertions cover both losing interleavings, destruction and orphaning.

Currently: `--- FAIL`, 235 corrupt-hook reports, ~2s. Fails 3/3 runs at `GOMAXPROCS=1` and `2` under `-race`, so it won't go quiet on a small CI runner. I got there by measurement, not guesswork: 8 installers on one hook only reproduced 2/24 rounds, and *more* goroutines made it rarer; seeding all five specs at 4 installers is what made it near-deterministic (measured per-round rates ~5% at 1 CPU, ~25% at 2, ~60% at 4).

**A correction to the fix I gave you.** I verified the test can go green, and my earlier `link(2)` suggestion is wrong — it makes things worse. `os.Link` + `os.Remove` leaves a window where the hook and its backup share one inode, and `writeHookFile`'s in-place `O_TRUNC` then reaches through into the backup: every round corrupted, all five hooks, versus ~60% before. What actually works is backing the hook up as a **copy** created with `O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_EXCL` (the bytes are already in hand from the `existing` read, and `EEXIST` means another installer got there first, so its backup is left intact), plus re-deriving `backupExists` via `fileExists(backupPath)` right before choosing chained-vs-plain content. With that patch the new test passes 3/3 at `GOMAXPROCS=2` and `4` under `-race`, and the whole `strategy` suite is green (42s). I reverted the fix so the test stays RED — the diff is at `scratchpad/candidate-fix.diff` if you want it.

All four properties landed: 4 installers, every `ManagedGitHookNames()` entry seeded, 60 fresh-repo rounds as subtests, and the chain assertion that catches the orphan interleaving the old assertions structurally couldn't see. Cost is 5.4s plain / 6.5s under `-race`, which is proportionate for a data-loss guard. Full `strategy` suite green (127s, most of it pre-existing), lint clean, worktree clean.

I deleted my own duplicate `hooks_concurrent_install_test.go` — their version now covers strictly more than mine did, and two 60-plus-round concurrency tests in one package is wasted CI time.

Trail #1012 has **no open findings**. Across the six passes, everything filed is now either fixed on this branch, verified as handled upstack in split B/C, or dismissed with evidence.

One nit I didn't file, since it's pre-existing rather than from this commit: `gitHookNames` (line 27) and `buildHookSpecs` (its own five `name:` literals) are two independent lists of the same five hooks, and the new test now depends on them agreeing. Add a hook to `buildHookSpecs` only and it gets installed but never raced by the test; add it to `gitHookNames` only and the test fails with a confusing "backup missing". Deriving the specs from `gitHookNames` would remove that coupling. Say the word and I'll file it or fix it.
